events.text:
🔍📹Pentagon budget reveals first new US nuclear bomb designation since Cold War
The Senate Appropriations Committee has disclosed the designation for the newest air-dropped nuclear gravity bomb prototype, the B94, according to a TWZ report.
The weapon is believed to be intended to destroy bunkers buried deep underground, with authorities requesting roughly $77 million in funding. The only weapon fitting that description that is known to be in development is the Nuclear Deterrent System-Air-delivered, or NDS-A.
The B94 development follows the W93 warhead for Trident II missiles. Before it, the last new nuclear bomb to receive a designation was the B90, a nuclear depth and strike bomb canceled in September 1991 as the Soviet Union collapsed.
The current US stockpile has one bomb specifically designed for deeply buried targets, [the B61-11](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77236), with a reported yield of 340 to 400 kilotons and fewer than 100 units in service. NDS-A could be planned as a potential replacement, though no further details were provided.
The recent war in Iran has become the reference case for conventional targeting limits. Iran's Pickaxe Mountain site turned out to be too deep and too hardened for non-nuclear penetrators, and the US stockpile of conventional bunker-busting munitions has been significantly depleted by sustained operations in [the Middle East](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76452).
The B94 is part of a broader modernization of the US nuclear triad that includes new air- and sea-launched nuclear cruise missiles, the Sentinel ICBM, the B-21 bomber, and the Columbia-class submarine program.

events.text:
🇮🇱 'Nvidia effect' doubles Israel's economic growth
Israel's economy grew at an annualized 8% in the third quarter, beating forecasts. But roughly half of that figure came from "overseas production," revenue traced back to Nvidia's taxes. Without it, the economy would have grown by only 3.4%, according to Bloomberg.
👉 Nvidia's presence in Israel began with Mellanox, the semiconductor firm it acquired in 2020 and turned into a major engineering hub. The intellectual property developed there stayed attributed to Israel, so a share of Nvidia's chip revenue lands in Israel's national accounts, even though the chips are fabricated elsewhere. The company employs about 6,000 people in Israel and has become the country's largest revenue-generating operation by a wide margin.
However, the AI boom that made the Nvidia effect possible is the same thing that makes Israel's headline growth vulnerable to a single company's fortunes. Jensen Huang's [resignation](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77728?single) last week sent Nvidia's shares plunging, potentially disrupting the flow of tax revenue to Israel as well. Beyond that, this revenue does little to boost local investment or job creation, analysts stress.

events.text:
👹 Netanyahu’s office, Shin Bet and Likud under spotlight over alleged election interference
Israeli police and the attorney general are reportedly investigating efforts by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office to undermine the election, The Times of Israel reports, providing further details.
🌏 Netanyahu’s chief of staff, Ido Norden, accused Ra’am activists of buying votes and alerted police ahead of the October 27 election. Acting solely on his information, 14 officers raided the homes of three Bedouin men in southern Israel without warrants. All three were arrested, but the investigation produced no substantive evidence or indictments. The raids nevertheless were later used by Netanyahu to challenge the election results. Netanyahu's office denies the allegations.
🌏 On election day, domestic intelligence agency Shin Bet's chief David Zini sought authorization to wiretap five Arab lawmakers over alleged foreign interference in the vote. The Attorney General’s Office rejected the request. Yet the foreign-interference allegation surfaced publicly just two days after Zini’s attempt with Central Elections Committee Chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg officially asking the Shin Bet to investigate the matter in the wake of the vote
🌏 The Shin Bet chief subsequently approached Gadi Eisenkot, head of the Yashar party and Netanyahu’s leading rival, declaring that “since 2018, the Arabs have been stealing the election in Israel” and adding that this would be the last time
🌏 The recent revelations shed new light on earlier controversy reported by The Times of Israel. The newspaper, citing unnamed security sources, reported that the Shin Bet had launched an investigation into alleged foreign interference in the election days, or even weeks, before the allegation was made public
🌏 Netanyahu’s Likud party and its coalition allies sought to prevent the ratification and certification of the election results to stop President Isaac Herzog from tasking Eisenkot with forming a new government, according to media reports. Likud is still preparing to appeal the election results, with the deadline for filing an appeal set for November 18.
